newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian lira strengthens past 1,000/mark barrier.
newsitem.headline: Italian lira strengthens past 1,000/mark barrier.

text.p: The Italian lira strengthened past the 1,000 per mark barrier in early trade helped by a stronger dollar and lower than expected preliminary inflation data for March, dealers said.
The lira was quoted at 998.60/8.90 per mark by 0815 GMT after trading at 1,002.35 late on Thursday, before inflation data came out.

Seven cities' data show March CPI running at 0.1 percent month-on-month and 2.2 percent year-on-year, which, if confirmed by four more cities' data later today, will be lower than analysts' forecasts of 2.3 percent and February's 2.4 percent.
"Inflation was really positive, it helped Btps and the lira a lot," one currency trader said.
Uncertainty remains in the market, however, with players waiting to know details of the government's proposed mini-budget for 1997.

Italian media reported late on Thursday the package would be for 15.0-15.5 trillion lire worth of budget deficit cuts but what areas of state accounts the measures will affect is not yet definite. This uncertainty helped drive the lira down to four month lows at 1,007.30 this week.
"We have to see if the market believes in the mini budget because there's still uncertainty over half of its contents," a dealer said.
"This is a good level to buy (marks) and there could be some profit-taking. But with the positive factors of the CPI and the budget the damage will be limited," he added.
